title: Evaluation of three methods for betanin quantification in fruits from cacti
author: Sandate-Flores, Rodríguez-Hernández, et al.

steps.title: Collect and store cactus fruit pulp
steps.instruction: Collect batches of fruits: chico (10 kg) and pitaya de mayo (collected in Ahuatlán, 18° 34′ N, 98° 15′ W, Puebla, processed within 48 h of harvest); garambullo (3 kg) from Ahualulco, 22° 24′ N, 101° 10′ W, San Luis Potosí, processed within 24 h of harvest; and jiotilla (22 kg) from Santa Maria Zoquitlán, 16° 33′ N, 96° 23′ W, Oaxaca, processed within 24 h of harvest. Perform all processing at the Water Center of Tecnológico de Monterrey. Wash fruits with tap water and Extran MA05 (Merck, Item 1400001403, Lot Mx1400005004, Estado de México, México). Manually remove prickles, separate peel and pulp, and remove seeds using a juice extractor (Model TU05, Turmix MR, Estado de México, México). Store seed‑free pulp in 100 mL low‑density polyethylene Ziploc® bags at –18 °C and use the samples within 15 days after thawing at room temperature (25 ± 2 °C).

steps.title: Extract pigments from pulp
steps.instruction: For each fruit type prepare fifteen samples. Defrost the stored pulp, weigh 5 g of pulp for each sample and place it in a 40 mL vial. Add 10 mL of Milli‑Q water, then agitate the mixture for 15 min. Filter the suspension under dark conditions through Whatman paper grade 4 (150 mm, Item 1009150, GE Healthcare Life Sciences, Little Chalfont, UK). Wash the filter with 30 mL of Milli‑Q water and finally bring the filtrate to the 50 mL mark. Determine moisture gravimetrically to express analyte concentration on a dry‑weight basis.

steps.title: Dilute extracts for analysis
steps.instruction: Dilute the crude extracts with Milli‑Q water as follows: garambullo, jiotilla and chico extracts 2‑fold; pitaya de mayo extract 5‑fold.

steps.title: Prepare fortified validation samples
steps.instruction: For each fruit type prepare ten fortified samples (five prepared by analyst 1 and five by analyst 2). Add 0.2 mL of a stock solution of known concentration to a 1 mL volumetric flask, then fill the flask to the mark with the corresponding cactus fruit extract. Transfer the resulting solution to a 5 mL volumetric flask and fill to the mark with Milli‑Q water.
